Lita.name: Lita
Lita.personality: Cheerful (you will always see her smiling!).
Lita.curiousFact: She has her own orchard and likes to encase herself in her shell, like a ball.

Duba.name: Duba
Duba.personality: Hungry (it's always a great time to eat!).
Duba.curiousFact: Her favorite dish is beefsteak and she loves to make "asados".

Yvoty.name: Yvoty
Yvoty.personality: Creative. Unprejudiced (she doesn't mind what people think!).
Yvoty.curiousFact: Yvoty means "flower" in the Guaraní language and is pronounced "ivotí", with the stress on the last "i". But it is written with two "y"!

Manic.name: Mañic
Manic.personality: Curious. Active. Agile (she never forgets her inline skates!).
Manic.curiousFact: Her grandmother from Formosa (Argentina) gave her the name, which literally means "ñandú" in the Qom language.

Capy.name: Capy y Guyrá
Capy.definition: the capybara and the cattle tyrant
Capy.curiousFact: Their names Capy (from "capybara" which means "lord of the grass") and Guyrá (means "bird"), are from the Tupi Guaraní language.

Chuy.name: Chuy
Chuy.personality: Generose. Sportsperson (they love to climb sea cliffs!).
Chuy.curiousFact: Their name comes from "chuy chuy" which means "cold" in the Mapuche language.

board.title: 1. Build the scene
board.text: Drag pieces from the palette onto the board, or tap a piece and then a cell. Drag across several cells to paint them at once.

texts.title: 2. Say what it is about
texts.text: Write the title and the statement above the board. Then choose the blocks the student will have and, if you like, the assessments.

try.title: 3. Try it and share it
try.text: Choose "Editor with preview" to play the challenge while you build it. When the publish checklist is complete, share it or download it.

solver.title: Recommended solution
solver.solved: It can be solved! This solution uses {{blocks}} blocks.
solver.notShortest: It is one possible solution: it is not guaranteed to be the shortest.
solver.rawSteps: Before optimizing it had {{steps}} instructions, one step at a time.
solver.notExact: There are many objects: the route is good, but it may not be the shortest.
solver.notAllScenarios: This solution does not work for every scenario. A single program for different scenarios needs conditionals: the notes explain why it could not be built.
solver.warningsTitle: Assessments this solution does not meet

warnings.mainTooLong: The main program has {{count}} instructions; with maximum length {{max}} up to {{allowed}} are accepted.
warnings.procedureTooLong: “{{name}}” has {{count}} instructions; with maximum length {{max}} up to {{allowed}} are accepted.
warnings.nestedControl: There is a repetition inside another one in {{name}}.
warnings.noRepetition: It does not use simple repetition.
warnings.needsConditionalRepetition: It does not use conditional repetition.
warnings.needsConditionalAlternative: It does not use a conditional alternative.

reasons.nothingRepeats: The route has no repeated steps.
reasons.noLandmark: No stretch ends at a border, an obstacle or an object that a toolbox sensor can detect.
reasons.nothingToDecide: There is nothing to decide on this board: an “If” needs several scenarios where the same cell sometimes has an object and sometimes does not.
reasons.incompatibleScenarios: The scenarios have different sizes or the character starts in different places, and a common program is not calculated in that case yet.
reasons.notYet: It is not calculated automatically yet.

notes.paddleNotRequired: Paddles are not required to win and “Pick paddle” is not in the toolbox: this solution does not pick them up.
notes.chargerNotRequired: Chargers are not required when every cellphone is unlocked and “Pick charger” is not in the toolbox: this solution does not pick them up.
notes.untilWithOneScenario: With a single scenario, “Repeat N times” would also work; the condition keeps the program working if the board changes.
notes.commonProgram: One program solves the {{scenarios}} scenarios: it uses sensors to ask where the objects are.
notes.scenariosIncompatible: The scenarios cannot be solved with one program (different size, different start, or obstacles where another has objects): the solution is for the scenario you are editing.
notes.commonNeedsBlocks: For one program to solve every scenario, the toolbox needs: {{blocks}}.
